newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung says would legalise Communist Party. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung says would legalise Communist Party. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]

text.p: The man tipped to become Hong Kong's future leader, tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, said on Tuesday he would legalise the Communist Party in the territory if he was asked to after the British colony reverts to China next year.

"Certainly yes," Tung replied to a reporter's question at a news conference after he had addressed the World Economic Forum. He had been asked if it would be okay with him to legalise the party. (Corrects from "to legalise the currently outlawed party" to clarify that the current status of the party is not clear.)
All political parties were outlawed in Hong Kong by the British colonial authorities until reforms in 1990. The status of the Chinese Communist Party remains a grey area.

However, the party was strictly illegal before that, and had been involved in violent conflicts with the colonial government, especially during the bloody Hong Kong riots of 1967 inspired by China's radical left-wing Cultural Revolution.
"I think there are Communist Party members in Hong Kong now," Tung said. "Indeed they will continue to be here. I do not know what their own plans are, whether they want to be legalised or not."
